[Session 01 | Ticket MIG-1007] Engineering sync for Project Atlas migration wave 1. Subsystem focus: service_mesh (Envoy 1.29 sidecar proxy with mTLS strict mode). During the canary rollout window, telemetry recorded p99 latency of 26ms at 1609 req/sec across three availability zones. Memory utilization remained bounded below 68% of container cgroup limits with zero OOMKill events observed during the 4-hour soak test.

Architecture review notes for MIG-1007: Service dependencies were validated against the updated contract schema. Backward compatibility shims remain active for legacy v1 REST consumers while gRPC protobuf definitions are pinned to release tag v2.1.0. Automated runbooks in PagerDuty have been updated with new alert thresholds for error budget burn rates exceeding 2% over a rolling 1-hour window.

Operational checklist for service_mesh in session 01: 1) Verify Terraform state lock in DynamoDB prior to applying module changes; 2) Confirm read-replica lag remains under 150ms during schema migration step; 3) Validate IAM OIDC workload identity federation bindings for service account atlas-worker-01; 4) Archive pre-migration heap profiles and flamegraphs to the compliance audit bucket for quarterly SOC2 review.

Post-deployment verification log (MIG-1007): Synthetic canary probes executed 14,400 health checks with 99.993% success rate. Connection pool exhaustion tests confirmed graceful backpressure via HTTP 429 Retry-After headers when upstream concurrency exceeded 512 active streams. Rollback automation was dry-run tested in staging and completed state restoration within 42 seconds.

Detailed capacity planning appendix for Wave 1 (Session 01): Baseline CPU reservations were tuned from 1500m down to 1200m per replica across the 16-node Kubernetes cluster, reclaiming 4.8 vCPUs per availability zone without degrading tail latency. Network egress metrics confirmed that zstd payload compression reduced cross-AZ data transfer volume by 34.2% during peak reconciliation windows.

Security and compliance sign-off notes (MIG-1007): Static application security testing (SAST) and container image vulnerability scanning via Trivy reported zero critical or high CVEs in base image distroless/static-debian12. Mutual TLS certificate lifetimes are enforced at 24 hours via cert-manager CSI driver with automated rotation.

SRE handoff summary for MIG-1007 (Session 01): Distributed tracing sampling rate is fixed at 10% for baseline traffic and 100% for anomalous HTTP 5xx responses or slow RPCs exceeding 250ms. Chaos engineering fault-injection experiments verified zero data loss during simulated rack switch partitioning across availability zones.
